findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: Upon arrival, there weren’t any employees who were food manager certified. Shortly throughout the visit, a CFPM arrived to correct the violation. Ensure that there is always an employee present who holds a manger’s certification if operating during business hours.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: There were at least two containers of salad dressings that lacked proper date marking inside of the dressing cooler. The items included tartar sauce and chipotle mayonnaise. Discussed with the PIC that in house dressings require date marking if being cold held longer than 24 hours. Ensure that dressings are date marked to make sure that they are getting used within the seven day timeframe.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed single service to go containers stored with the food contact surfaces not inverted. Discussed with the PIC and the containers were properly inverted to correct the violation. Ensure that food contact surfaces are always faced downward to protect against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following areas are in need of cleaning:
- Floor under dish machine’s drainboard was observed with accumulated food debris
- Floor in back-stock area (where bread rack is stored) was observed with accumulated food debris
Be sure to sweep the above mentioned areas as frequent as necessary to keep them clean.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment:
Cooler still not fixed from the July 8, 2026 inspection.
The drawer cooler across from the cookline was observed with an ambient temperature of 57F-60F. The facility does not keep a record log and the employees were unaware of when the cooler stopped working. See that the unit is serviced to maintain proper cold holding temperatures of 41F of below. The employees were instructed to not use the cooler until it is serviced. Will follow-up on July 24, 2026.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: There wasn’t a certified food protection manager present despite the facility being in full operation. The PIC mentioned that she is working to become a CFPM pretty soon. Ensure that there is always CFPM available during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The sanitizer solution along the cookline was observed with a concentration of 0ppm (CL). The employees mentioned that the solution was prepared early in the morning. Discussed frequently changing sani solutions, as the solution loses its concentration the longer it sits. The solution was remade and tested at 100ppm (CL) to correct the violation. Ensure that sani solutions are maintained at the manufacturer's recommended concentration and are switched roughly every 4 hours (or if soiled).
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: There was residue starting to form on the baffles of the ice machine. Shown to the PIC. Suggested cleaning ice baffles as frequent as necessary to keep them clean. Ensure that baffles are cleaned to prevent accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.11(E) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (E) Except when dry cleaning methods are used as specified under § 4-603.11, surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting FOOD that is not TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cleaned: (1) At any time when contamination may have occurred; (2) At least every 24 hours for iced tea dispensers and CONSUMER self service UTENSILS such as tongs, scoops, or ladles; (3) Before restocking CONSUMER self-service EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS such as condiment dispensers and display containers; and (4) In EQUIPMENT such as ice bins and BEVERAGE dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of EQUIPMENT such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, BEVERAGE and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending EQUIPMENT: (a) At a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or (b) Absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: There were various time/temperature control foods (TCS) stored inside of a nonfunctional drawer cooler with an internal temperature of 57F-60F. The PIC mentioned that the foods were placed inside of the cooler at 9am. The facility was instructed to discard foods due to being held well above 41F. Violation corrected. The ambient temperature of the kitchen was above 75F degrees and the extreme heat could be exhausting the drawer coolers. See that the cooler is serviced to maintain proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The drawer cooler across from the cookline was observed with an ambient temperature of 57F-60F. The facility does not keep a record log and the employees were unaware of when the cooler stopped working. See that the unit is serviced to maintain proper cold holding temperatures of 41F of below. The employees were instructed to not use the cooler until it is serviced. Will follow-up on July 21, 2026.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed no paper towels to be present at bar hand sink. Discussed with PIC, paper towels were moved to hand sink. Ensure all hand sinks are properly equipped with paper towels and soap.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed the following locations to be soiled with food debris:
1) The microwave in the cook line was observed to be soiled with significant food debris.
2) The top of the ice machine was observed to have a small amount of food debris that is not in contact with ice openings. Ensure area is cleaned. 

Discussed with PIC, the following areas will be cleaned. Ensure non food contact surfaces are being cleaned at a frequency that prevents food debris accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There was ice observed in the handwashing sink by the dish area from a drink being dumped in it. CORRECTED- Educated PIC that handwashing sinks can only be used for the intended purpose of handwashing. Handwashing sinks cannot be used as a dump sink or for any other purpose.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: There are multiple clear containers of food that have been removed from its package in dry storage that does not have a label on it. Ensure that these containers are labeled with the common name of the food.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
The following nonfood contact surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The fans of both clear door coolers in the kitchen. 
2. The fans in the walk-in cooler. 
3. The nonfood contact surfaces of both soda machines. 
4. The dessert chest freezer in the kitchen needs to be de-frosted to allow it to be smooth and easily cleanable. 

Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following physical facilities need to be repaired: 

1. There is a frost issue in the walk-in freezer that is causing frost/ice build up on the shelves, floor, and door. Ensure that this issue is repaired and the ice is scraped off to allow these surfaces to be smooth and easily cleanable. 
2. The back prep table needs caulked to the wall. 
3. FIRST REPEAT- Behind the ice machine needs to be sealed, as there is paint that is peeling. Ensure that this is sealed and made to be smooth and easily cleanable. 
4. FIRST REPEAT- The table to the right of the soda machine in the kitchen needs to be caulked to the wall. Ensure that this is caulked and made to be smooth and easily cleanable. 

Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.
